text:
clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir los usos de la tecnología digital para la salud item/776ee926-430a-4031-891b-83788c96f724 10665-379033 organización mundial de la salud  2024-09-24   classification technology medical informatics telemedicine health services digital health esta segunda edición de la clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud proporciona una taxonomía normalizada para describir cómo se utilizan las tecnologías digitales para responder a las necesidades de las personas y de los sistemas de salud. desarrollada por la oms, la clasificación establece un lenguaje común destinado a facilitar la comunicación entre responsables de la formulación de políticas, gestores de programas de salud, investigadores, implementadores, desarrolladores tecnológicos y otras partes interesadas en la salud digital. organiza las intervenciones de salud digital en torno a capacidades tecnológicas específicas diseñadas para abordar desafíos de los sistemas de salud y las vincula con los servicios digitales y los tipos de aplicaciones mediante los cuales se prestan.

title: Classification of Digital Health Interventions v1.0
abstract: This publication presents version 1.0 of the World Health Organization’s Classification of Digital Health Interventions (DHIs), a taxonomy developed to provide a shared and standardized language for describing how digital and mobile technol
text:
classification of digital health interventions v1.0 item/98c528f1-48f0-4803-9a11-c83cd2e52c17 who-rhr-1806-eng world health organization who/rhr/18.06 2018-03-14  1. headquarters classification technology medical informatics telemedicine digital health this publication presents version 1.0 of the world health organization’s classification of digital health interventions (dhis), a taxonomy developed to provide a shared and standardized language for describing how digital and mobile technologies are used to address health system needs. intended primarily for public health audiences, the framework supports communication among policymakers, programme planners, implementers, researchers, donors and technology specialists by defining digital health interventions as discrete digital functionalities linked to specific health objectives. the classification was developed to facilitate evidence synthesis, landscape analyses, planning processes and the articulation of digital solutions to identified health system challenges.

the framework organizes digital health interventions into four primary groups according to the main user: clients, health-care providers, health system managers and data services. it links digital interventions to broader health system challenges and to system categories such as electronic medical records, logistics management information systems and telemedicine platforms. developed through technical consultations, literature review and public feedback, the classification builds on existing mhealth and ehealth frameworks while providing a simplified and practical reference for health programmes. the document is intended to support the design, implementation, evaluation and interoperability of digital health initiatives and will be periodically updated to reflect emerging technologies and evolving practices in digital health.

abstract: These consolidated guidelines provide comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations for HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and programme monitoring across the continuum of HIV care. Updating the 2016 WHO consolidated guide
text:
consolidated guidelines on hiv prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring: recommendations for a public health approach item/1c992591-c558-4371-a07c-d243f65ef1d4  world health organization  2021-07-16   hiv infections risk factors vulnerable populations guideline anti-retroviral agents these consolidated guidelines provide comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations for hiv prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and programme monitoring across the continuum of hiv care. updating the 2016 who consolidated guidelines, this edition integrates guidance issued between 2016 and 2021 and reflects major advances in clinical practice, diagnostics and service delivery. developed using the grade approach and informed by expert consultation and country experience, the guidelines aim to support countries in implementing high-quality, person-centred hiv services while advancing universal health coverage and progress towards ending aids as a public health threat by 2030.

the publication addresses hiv testing strategies, prevention interventions, antiretroviral therapy, management of advanced hiv disease, care for common coinfections and comorbidities, differentiated service delivery, procurement, laboratory services and programme monitoring. it incorporates updated recommendations on hiv self-testing, pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis, dolutegravir-based treatment, rapid antiretroviral therapy initiation, viral load monitoring and community-based models of care. intended primarily for national hiv programme managers, policy-makers and health-care providers, the guidelines also serve as a resource for technical partners, community organizations and people living with hiv to support the implementation of effective, equitable and people-centred hiv programmes.

text:
consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing hiv infection: recommendations for a public health approach item/e1d59705-e50f-4e1a-b344-0c8a2ec8003b  world health organization  2016-06-06   hiv infections anti-retroviral agents guideline this evidence-based guideline consolidates world health organization recommendations on the use of antiretroviral (arv) drugs for treating and preventing hiv infection, providing a comprehensive public health framework for hiv diagnosis, prevention, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring and evaluation across all age groups and populations. developed in response to advances in scientific evidence and evolving programmatic needs, the second edition updates the 2013 consolidated guidelines and incorporates new recommendations, including universal eligibility for antiretroviral therapy (art) regardless of cd4 cell count, expanded use of pre-exposure prophylaxis, and optimized approaches to hiv testing, treatment monitoring and management of coinfections and comorbidities. the guideline also outlines the methods used for guideline development and the principles underpinning a public health approach.

title: Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran
meta: Khadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; Sussan Mahmoody; Seyed Mohsen Zahraie; Maziar Moradi-Lakeh; Sedigheh R. Tabatabaei; Abdollah Karimi · 2019-10-29
abstract:
Background:
Pneumococcal disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae results in considerable mortality and morbidity. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV), such as PCV-13, can prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and avoid disability and d
text:
cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the islamic republic of iran item/638b31e3-ec3e-424c-ac12-53d5ed2fdb73 10665-385346 khadijeh ezoji mohsen yaghoubi marzieh nojomi sussan mahmoody seyed mohsen zahraie maziar moradi-lakeh sedigheh r. tabatabaei abdollah karimi  2019-10-29   pneumococcal infections pneumococcal vaccines vaccination health care costs health expenditures background:
pneumococcal disease caused by streptococcus pneumoniae results in considerable mortality and morbidity. pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (pcv), such as pcv-13, can prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and avoid disability and death. the cost of introducing pcv-13 in childhood immunization schedules should be assessed against the cost of pneumococcal diseases for each community.
aims:
this study aimed to evaluate the cost–effectiveness of introducing pcv-13 in the national immunization programme for children under 5 years in the islamic republic of iran.
methods:
the trivac decision support model was used to estimate total costs of introducing pcv-13 and the disability-adjusted life years (dalys)averted. the main pneumococcal diseases were considered—pneumonia, meningitis, acute otitis media, and non-pneumonia, non-meningitis infections—in terms of hospital admissions, outpatient visits and deaths. local data were used to estimate costs.
results:
pneumococcal disease is estimated to affect 18 713 211 children under 5 years (519 412 pneumonia, 18 148 116 acute otitis media, 6884 meningitis, and 38 799 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis)in 10 years (2014–2023)without use of the vaccine. introduction of pcv-13 would prevent 4 900 084 cases of pneumococcal disease (190 849 pneumonia, 4 692 450 acute otitis media, 2529 meningitis, and 14 256 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis). pneumococcal infection would cause 287 950 hospital admissions and 29 399 deaths; vaccination could avert 105 802 hospital admissions and 9997 deaths. the incremental cost–effectiveness was estimated to be us$ 1890 and us$ 1538 per averted daly for the government and society respectively.
conclusion:
according to who-recommended thresholds for interpreting cost–effectiveness, introduction of pcv-13 for children under 5 years in the islamic republic of iran would be cost-effective

abstract: Este documento presenta las recomendaciones de la OMS, basadas en la evidencia, sobre el uso de intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud y apoyar el avance hacia la cobertura sanitaria universal (CSU). Elaborada en res
text:

text: enumeration of cd4 t lymphocytes : report of a workshop, bangkok, thailand, 6-10 june 2006 item/6804fe89-6428-45f8-9e42-95097eb5e1cf 10665-205022 world health organization. regional office for south-east asia sea-hlm-390 2006-12-31    description: enumeration of cd4 t lymphocytes is essential for initiation of antiretroviral therapy for a person with hiv as well as for monitoring the response to treatment. the techniques for enumeration of cd4 t lymphocytes are evolving. the flow cytometry continues to be the gold standard of cd4 t lymphocytes enumeration in spite of the fact that the technology is expensive both in terms of initial investment in sophisticated equipment and running cost. the newer techniques may be economical to procure and maintain. the latter are particularly intended for countries with limited resources. who conducted a workshop to orient the nationals about these technologies and integration of a quality system into routine testing, at siriraj hospital bangkok. the report describes the status of cd4 testing in these countries. while indonesia, india and thailand have developed a good infrastructure for enumeration of cd4 t lymphocytes, bangladesh, myanmar, nepal and sri lanka have made a beginning in this direction. the workshop focussed on principles of various techniques and imparted a hands-on training for performing the same. the issues regarding selection of technology, procurement of equipment and their maintenance; ensuring continuous supply and economical use of reagents and biosafety in laboratory were discussed and have been presented in this report.

abstract: La Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 proporciona un marco para apoyar a los Estados Miembros en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de salud mediante la adopción y el uso adecuados de las tecnologías digitales. Elaborada en re
text:
estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 item/2da90ddf-7e77-409f-86ab-a34497747b2d 10665-344251 organización mundial de la salud  2021-08-18   health information systems digital technology strategic planning telemedicine medical informatics digital health la estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 proporciona un marco para apoyar a los estados miembros en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de salud mediante la adopción y el uso adecuados de las tecnologías digitales. elaborada en respuesta a los mandatos de la asamblea mundial de la salud y alineada con los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible y las metas de los “tres mil millones” de la oms, la estrategia establece una visión compartida para mejorar la salud y el bienestar a través de soluciones de salud digital accesibles, asequibles, seguras y sostenibles. destaca la importancia de una gobernanza sólida, la interoperabilidad, el uso ético de los datos, la protección de la privacidad, el fortalecimiento de las capacidades del personal sanitario y la inversión en infraestructura digital para apoyar las prioridades nacionales de salud y la cobertura sanitaria universal.

el documento define cuatro objetivos estratégicos: promover la colaboración mundial y el intercambio de conocimientos; avanzar en la implementación de estrategias nacionales de salud digital; fortalecer la gobernanza de la salud digital a nivel mundial, regional y nacional; y fomentar sistemas de salud centrados en las personas mediante el uso de tecnologías digitales. asimismo, presenta principios rectores, un marco de implementación y mecanismos de seguimiento destinados a apoyar a los países en el desarrollo de ecosistemas de salud digital interoperables. se presta especial atención a los obstáculos que enfrentan los países de ingresos bajos y medianos y a garantizar que la transformación digital contribuya a sistemas de salud más equitativos, eficaces y resilientes.

abstract: This guidance document provides updated World Health Organization criteria and processes for validating the elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B virus (HBV) as public health priorities. Buildi
text:
global guidance on criteria and processes for validation: elimination of mother-to-child transmission of hiv, syphilis and hepatitis b virus item/caa49deb-2f22-4797-979e-51afb11f869b 10665-349550 world health organization  2021-11-25   hiv infections syphilis infectious disease transmission, vertical maternal health services child women hepatitis b virus infant, newborn guideline this guidance document provides updated world health organization criteria and processes for validating the elimination of mother-to-child transmission (emtct) of hiv, syphilis and hepatitis b virus (hbv) as public health priorities. building on previous editions focused on hiv and syphilis, this third version incorporates validation guidance for hbv within the framework of the triple elimination initiative. the document outlines standardized indicators, targets and assessment procedures for evaluating progress towards emtct across diverse epidemiological and programmatic settings. it addresses impact and process indicators, surveillance and laboratory quality standards, programme assessment, and requirements related to human rights, gender equality and community engagement.

the document emphasizes integrated maternal and child health approaches, universal access to quality antenatal and prevention services, and the importance of strong health systems and surveillance mechanisms. it also provides guidance for countries with high disease burdens through the path to elimination framework, as well as for countries with small numbers of affected pregnant women and special populations. intended for national, regional and global validation bodies, the document supports harmonized validation processes while allowing countries to pursue single, dual or triple emtct validation according to national readiness and regional priorities.

title: Global hepatitis report 2026
abstract: This report provides a comprehensive assessment of the global burden of viral hepatitis and progress towards the goal of eliminating hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. Drawing on data reported by Member States and modelled estimat
text:
global hepatitis report 2026 item/b89fc26c-9fdb-465a-ae3d-a325a35bd4e7 10665-385385 world health organization  2026-04-24   hepatitis b hepatitis c hepatitis, viral, human preventive health services public health surveillance health policy health planning delivery of health care incidence prevalence mortality this report provides a comprehensive assessment of the global burden of viral hepatitis and progress towards the goal of eliminating hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. drawing on data reported by member states and modelled estimates, it analyses trends in incidence, prevalence and mortality associated with hepatitis b and c, covering the period from 2015 to 2024 based on the latest available data. it also situates these trends within the context of global commitments, strategies and targets.

the publication reviews the coverage and impact of key interventions for prevention, diagnosis and treatment, including vaccination, infection prevention and control, harm reduction and access to antiviral therapies. it identifies persistent gaps in testing and treatment, marked regional disparities, and the need for accelerated scale-up of services, particularly in high-burden settings. the report concludes that progress towards the 2030 elimination targets remains off track despite the availability of effective interventions. intended for policymakers, programme managers and public health stakeholders, it serves as an analytical and strategic resource to guide national and global responses to viral hepatitis.

abstract: The Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 provides a framework to support Member States in strengthening health systems through the appropriate adoption and use of digital technologies. Developed in response to World Health Assembly m
text:
global strategy on digital health 2020-2025 item/bd23c952-ac42-4c82-b05d-d86e3228fe5a 10665-344249 world health organization  2021-08-18   health information systems digital technology strategic planning telemedicine medical informatics digital health the global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 provides a framework to support member states in strengthening health systems through the appropriate adoption and use of digital technologies. developed in response to world health assembly mandates and aligned with the sustainable development goals and who’s triple billion targets, the strategy outlines a shared vision for improving health and well-being through accessible, affordable, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. it emphasizes the importance of strong governance, interoperability, ethical use of data, privacy protection, workforce capacity-building and investment in digital infrastructure to support national health priorities and universal health coverage.

the document establishes four strategic objectives: promoting global collaboration and knowledge exchange; advancing the implementation of national digital health strategies; strengthening governance for digital health at global, regional and national levels; and advocating people-centred health systems enabled by digital technologies. it also presents guiding principles, an implementation framework and monitoring mechanisms to support countries in developing interoperable digital health ecosystems. particular attention is given to addressing barriers faced by low- and middle-income countries and ensuring that digital transformation contributes to equitable, effective and resilient health systems.

title: Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV
abstract: This guideline provides updated, evidence-informed recommendations for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV. Developed in accordance with WHO Guideline Review Commit
text:
guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with hiv item/a406080b-d37f-456d-9663-fe74b17a0e04 10665-357088 world health organization  2022-06-23   hiv infections meningitis, cryptococcal adult adolescent child guideline this guideline provides updated, evidence-informed recommendations for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with hiv. developed in accordance with who guideline review committee procedures, it replaces the 2018 guidance and incorporates important new evidence published in 2021 on the preferred antifungal induction regimen for cryptococcal meningitis. the recommendations are based on systematic reviews using the grade approach and are supported by considerations of acceptability, values and preferences, feasibility and cost–effectiveness. the document addresses cryptococcal disease as a major opportunistic infection contributing substantially to hiv-related illness, disability and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, and identifies priority knowledge gaps to inform future research.

the guideline recommends updated approaches to the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of cryptococcal disease, including revised guidance on induction therapy for cryptococcal meningitis, while maintaining earlier recommendations where evidence remains unchanged. it also outlines principles for implementation within a public health approach and is intended to support hiv programme managers, policy-makers, health-care professionals and people living with hiv in improving the prevention, early diagnosis and clinical management of cryptococcal disease.

abstract: This guideline provides evidence-informed recommendations on the use of long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention in people at substantial risk of HIV infection. Developed according t
text:
guidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for hiv prevention item/89df0258-5433-4616-a801-8668d6f20f64 10665-360869 world health organization  2022-07-27   hiv infections anti-hiv agents pre-exposure prophylaxis cabotegravir guideline this guideline provides evidence-informed recommendations on the use of long-acting injectable cabotegravir (cab-la) as pre-exposure prophylaxis (prep) for hiv prevention in people at substantial risk of hiv infection. developed according to who guideline development procedures, it is based on systematic reviews, grade assessments and additional evidence on effectiveness, safety, acceptability, feasibility, equity and cost–effectiveness. the document reviews the global hiv prevention context, the rationale for expanding hiv prevention choices, and the evidence supporting cab-la as an additional prep option. it also outlines the principles guiding implementation within a public health and human rights framework and identifies the intended audiences for the recommendations.

the guideline recommends that long-acting injectable cabotegravir may be offered as an additional hiv prevention choice as part of combination prevention approaches for people at substantial risk of hiv infection. it discusses key implementation considerations, including hiv testing, service delivery models, comprehensive prevention services, community engagement, provider training and adherence support. the publication also identifies priority research gaps related to safety, drug resistance, delivery strategies and population-level impact, and describes the guideline development process, dissemination strategy and supporting evidence underpinning the recommendation.

text:
guidelines: updated recommendations on hiv prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring item/396e27dd-8532-4243-b4b5-bff30eeebc1b 10665-340190 world health organization  2021-03-17   hiv infections clinical medicine guideline this guideline presents updated who recommendations on selected priority areas across the hiv prevention, diagnosis and treatment continuum, developed in response to emerging evidence, implementation experience and evolving clinical practice. prepared according to who guideline review committee procedures and informed by systematic reviews using the grade approach, it updates and complements the 2016 consolidated hiv guidelines. the publication addresses key public health challenges affecting the global hiv response, particularly in resource-limited settings, and supports progress towards ending aids as a public health threat by 2030 through a public health approach to service delivery.

title: Lignes directrices de l'OMS : recommandations sur les interventions numériques pour le renforcement des systèmes de santé
abstract: Ces lignes directrices de l’OMS présentent des recommandations fondées sur des données probantes concernant l’utilisation des interventions numériques pour renforcer les systèmes de santé et soutenir les progrès vers la couverture sanitaire
text:
lignes directrices de l'oms : recommandations sur les interventions numériques pour le renforcement des systèmes de santé item/780b5573-ba80-4b1a-9ce7-a50faf66a45a 10665-354400 organisation mondiale de la santé  2022-05-19   telemedicine guideline health services accessibility universal health insurance digital health ces lignes directrices de l’oms présentent des recommandations fondées sur des données probantes concernant l’utilisation des interventions numériques pour renforcer les systèmes de santé et soutenir les progrès vers la couverture sanitaire universelle (csu). élaborées en réponse à l’adoption croissante des technologies numériques et à la résolution sur la santé numérique approuvée par l’assemblée mondiale de la santé en 2018, elles répondent à la nécessité d’évaluer rigoureusement les interventions de santé numérique afin que les investissements reposent sur des données probantes relatives à leurs avantages, leurs inconvénients, leur acceptabilité, leur faisabilité, leurs implications en matière de ressources et les considérations d’équité. les lignes directrices soulignent que les technologies numériques doivent compléter, et non remplacer, les composantes fondamentales de systèmes de santé performants.

les recommandations portent sur un ensemble prioritaire d’interventions de santé numérique, principalement accessibles au moyen d’appareils mobiles, notamment la notification des naissances et des décès, la notification des stocks et la gestion des produits de base, la télémédecine entre client et prestataire ainsi qu’entre prestataires, la communication ciblée avec les clients, le suivi numérique de l’état de santé et des services reçus, les outils d’aide à la décision destinés aux professionnels de santé et l’apprentissage numérique. les lignes directrices présentent également des considérations relatives à la mise en œuvre, recensent les principales lacunes en matière de recherche et visent à aider les ministères de la santé, les responsables des politiques de santé, les professionnels de santé, les partenaires du développement et les autres parties prenantes à prendre des décisions éclairées concernant l’adoption, le déploiement à grande échelle et l’institutionnalisation des interventions de santé numérique efficaces.

title: National health workforce accounts: a handbook
abstract: This handbook introduces the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA), a standardized framework developed by the World Health Organization to strengthen health workforce information systems and support evidence-based workforce planning and
text:
national health workforce accounts: a handbook item/c8db7b21-da29-4432-a6d7-61ffe3b2c1c1 9789241513111-eng world health organization  2017-10-26  1. headquarters health personnel organizational objectives employment education, medical handbook universal health insurance this handbook introduces the national health workforce accounts (nhwa), a standardized framework developed by the world health organization to strengthen health workforce information systems and support evidence-based workforce planning and policy-making. the publication is intended to assist countries in monitoring and analysing health workforce capacity, distribution, education, labour market dynamics, financing, governance and information systems in the context of universal health coverage and the health-related sustainable development goals. it outlines the rationale for improved health workforce data and highlights the role of harmonized metrics in addressing challenges related to workforce availability, accessibility, performance and retention.

the handbook presents a modular framework comprising 78 core indicators organized across 10 modules covering active workforce stock, education and training, regulation and accreditation, education financing, labour market flows, employment conditions, workforce spending and remuneration, skill mix, governance, and health workforce information systems. for each indicator, it provides definitions, methodological guidance, reporting requirements, data sources and disaggregation options. the publication also describes implementation principles, reporting standards and potential applications of the nhwa, supporting countries in strengthening health workforce monitoring, facilitating international comparability and informing policies aimed at improving health system performance and population access to quality health services.

national health workforce accounts: a handbook item/c9312a35-1eeb-46be-8482-a5fd2a94ddb9 9789240081291-eng world health organization  2023-11-23  1. headquarters health personnel health workforce employment education, medical universal health insurance handbook the national health workforce accounts (nhwa) handbook, second edition, provides the conceptual framework, standards, methods and indicators that support the systematic collection, analysis and use of health workforce data for evidence-informed policy-making and planning. developed by the world health organization, the handbook supports implementation of the national health workforce accounts as a country-led system to strengthen human resources for health information systems, improve data quality and availability, and monitor progress towards universal health coverage, the sustainable development goals and other global health objectives. it describes the rationale, principles and applications of nhwa at national, regional and global levels and outlines a modular approach to health workforce monitoring.

the handbook presents guidance on implementation and reporting methods and defines a set of standardized indicators organized into four modules covering workforce stock and flows, education, finance and expenditures, and working conditions, governance and leadership. it explains indicator metadata, calculation methods, disaggregation requirements and reporting standards, and illustrates how nhwa data can be used to support workforce planning, policy development, retention strategies, equity analyses and monitoring of health workforce trends. the revised edition incorporates updated indicators, occupational classifications, tools and guidance to address evolving health workforce priorities and emerging global health challenges.

national health workforce accounts: health workforce levels and trends 2026 item/bb4009bc-943c-4116-88e3-fe4f6cf1a400 9789240122925-eng world health organization  2026-06-22  1. headquarters health workforce personnel staffing and scheduling health planning health status indicators health personnel personnel turnover age distribution demography population dynamics health resources data collection information systems national  health programs policy making workload forecasting health services needs and demand health services accessibility quality assurance, health care this report presents the 2026 edition of the national health workforce accounts (nhwa) series, providing an overview of the status of nhwa implementation and an analysis of global and regional health workforce levels and trends based on official data reported by countries to the world health organization. developed to support evidence-informed health workforce policy-making and planning, the report examines progress in strengthening national health workforce information systems, data availability and reporting across countries, and the use of standardized indicators to monitor human resources for health in support of universal health coverage, the sustainable development goals and other health objectives.

drawing on the 2025 nhwa data release, the report analyses the distribution, density and composition of the health and care workforce across regions and income groups, highlighting persistent disparities in workforce availability. it also examines trends in workforce growth since 2006 and presents a thematic analysis of population ageing and health workforce ageing, assessing their implications for future workforce needs. the findings demonstrate substantial improvements in the availability and quality of health workforce data through nhwa implementation while underscoring continuing challenges related to workforce shortages, inequities in distribution and the need for sustained investment in health workforce planning and monitoring.

abstract: The National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) Implementation Guide provides practical guidance for countries on establishing and sustaining systems to collect, analyse, use and report standardized health workforce data. Developed as a compa
text:
national health workforce accounts: implementation guide item/dc583bce-4e95-4e27-9b2e-7b98bbe8a144 9789241514446-eng world health organization  2018-10-19  1. headquarters health personnel organizational objectives employment education, medical universal health insurance the national health workforce accounts (nhwa) implementation guide provides practical guidance for countries on establishing and sustaining systems to collect, analyse, use and report standardized health workforce data. developed as a companion document to the nhwa handbook and in support of the global strategy on human resources for health: workforce 2030, the guide outlines a structured approach to strengthening health workforce information systems and improving the availability, quality and use of human resources for health data. it is intended for policy-makers, programme managers, technical experts and stakeholders involved in health workforce planning, monitoring and governance, and emphasizes collaboration across sectors such as health, education, labour, finance and statistics.

the guide presents an implementation framework organized into three phases—conceptualization, operationalization, and scaling up and sustainability—comprising eight steps that address political commitment, governance arrangements, planning, legal considerations, data compilation and analysis, validation, dissemination, and process review. it describes the roles of national institutions and multistakeholder coordination mechanisms, provides guidance on data quality, reporting and communication processes, and promotes the integration of existing information systems. by supporting the systematic monitoring of health workforce indicators, the guide aims to strengthen evidence-informed decision-making and contribute to health workforce development, universal health coverage and broader national and global health objectives.

title: Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025
abstract: La Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020–2025 fournit un cadre destiné à aider les États Membres à renforcer leurs systèmes de santé grâce à l’adoption et à l’utilisation appropriées des technologies numériques. Élaborée en répons
text:
stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025 item/7d0f8ec2-c315-4992-ac15-c07c63706ce7 10665-344250 organisation mondiale de la santé  2021-08-18   health information systems digital technology strategic planning medical informatics telemedicine digital health la stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020–2025 fournit un cadre destiné à aider les états membres à renforcer leurs systèmes de santé grâce à l’adoption et à l’utilisation appropriées des technologies numériques. élaborée en réponse aux mandats de l’assemblée mondiale de la santé et alignée sur les objectifs de développement durable ainsi que sur les objectifs du « triple milliard » de l’oms, cette stratégie présente une vision commune visant à améliorer la santé et le bien-être au moyen de solutions de santé numérique accessibles, abordables, sûres et durables. elle souligne l’importance d’une gouvernance solide, de l’interopérabilité, de l’utilisation éthique des données, de la protection de la vie privée, du renforcement des capacités des personnels de santé et des investissements dans les infrastructures numériques afin de soutenir les priorités nationales de santé et la couverture sanitaire universelle.

le document définit quatre objectifs stratégiques : promouvoir la collaboration mondiale et le partage des connaissances ; faire progresser la mise en œuvre des stratégies nationales de santé numérique ; renforcer la gouvernance de la santé numérique aux niveaux mondial, régional et national ; et promouvoir des systèmes de santé centrés sur les personnes grâce aux technologies numériques. il présente également des principes directeurs, un cadre de mise en œuvre et des mécanismes de suivi destinés à soutenir les pays dans le développement d’écosystèmes numériques interopérables. une attention particulière est accordée aux obstacles rencontrés par les pays à revenu faible ou intermédiaire et à la nécessité de veiller à ce que la transformation numérique contribue à des systèmes de santé plus équitables, efficaces et résilients.

the use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (tb-lamp) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance item/27e31e9f-fb42-45c7-affb-7fd72e901998 10665-249154 world health organization  2016-08-08   tuberculosis, pulmonary mycobacterium tuberculosis nucleic acid amplification techniques guideline tuberculosis remains a major global public health challenge, and the who end tb strategy emphasizes the need for early diagnosis and universal drug-susceptibility testing. this policy guidance presents evidence-based recommendations on the use of the commercial loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay (tb-lamp) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis. developed following a systematic review of studies conducted since 2012 and assessment using the grade approach, the document evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of tb-lamp as a replacement for sputum-smear microscopy, as an add-on test after negative smear microscopy, and in comparison with the xpert mtb/rif assay, while also assessing the frequency of indeterminate or invalid results.

abstract: This guidance document, part of the WHO Toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data, provides practical guidance on the integrated analysis and use of routine health information system (RHIS) data at district and health fac
text:
toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data: integrated health services analysis: district and facility level item/a013176b-cb29-41d1-bb3a-d2d4ef161cd3 10665-369381 world health organization  2023-06-16   health facilities data management health information systems health services this guidance document, part of the who toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data, provides practical guidance on the integrated analysis and use of routine health information system (rhis) data at district and health facility levels. it is intended to support managers, analysts and other health system stakeholders in monitoring health service delivery and using routine data for operational decision-making. the document promotes an integrated, standards-based approach that uses a limited set of tracer indicators representing multiple programmes and service components, thereby supporting primary health care, universal health coverage and the health-related sustainable development goals.

text:
understanding national health workforce accounts item/81b0f40b-5dbc-491d-a2ac-b63c7f3f9f27 who-his-hwf-nhwa-20171-eng world health organization who/his/hwf/nhwa/2017.1 2017-12-31  1. headquarters health personnel organizational objectives employment education, medical universal health insurance universal health insurance understanding national health workforce accounts (nhwa) is an introductory guidance document developed by the world health organization to explain the purpose, policy relevance and structure of the national health workforce accounts framework. the publication outlines how nhwa supports the standardization of health workforce information systems, improves the quality and comparability of data, and strengthens the evidence base for health workforce policy, planning and monitoring. positioned within the context of universal health coverage, the sustainable development goals, the global strategy on human resources for health: workforce 2030, and related international commitments, the document highlights the importance of reliable workforce information for addressing current and future health system challenges.

the publication describes the benefits of nhwa at national, regional and global levels and presents key policy questions that can be informed through systematic workforce data collection and analysis. it introduces the health labour market framework used by nhwa, emphasizing workforce production, labour market flows, distribution, productivity and regulation. the document also summarizes the development process of the nhwa indicators and explains the modular structure of the framework, which comprises ten modules covering workforce stock, education, labour market dynamics, employment conditions, financing, governance, planning and information systems. together, these elements provide a foundation for evidence-informed decision-making and strengthened health workforce monitoring.

title: Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement
abstract: This policy statement provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of commercial interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) for tuberculosis (TB) in low- and middle-income countries, particularly settings with a high TB and/or HIV burden
text:
use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (igras) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement item/ae4ae4f8-9322-4c48-9833-7a08aca631ef 10665-44759 world health organization  2011-12-31   interferon-gamma tuberculosis, pulmonary immunoassay reagent kits, diagnostic developing countries guideline this policy statement provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of commercial interferon-gamma release assays (igras) for tuberculosis (tb) in low- and middle-income countries, particularly settings with a high tb and/or hiv burden. based on systematic reviews and grade assessment, it evaluates igras for diagnosis of active tb, detection of latent tb infection (ltbi) in children and people living with hiv, screening of health care workers and contacts, outbreak investigations, and prediction of progression to active disease.

the evidence was generally of low or very low quality and did not demonstrate superior performance of igras over the tuberculin skin test (tst). who recommends that igras and the tst not be used to diagnose active tb or identify individuals at risk of developing active disease, and that igras not replace the tst for ltbi diagnosis in children, people living with hiv, or contacts. given comparable performance, greater cost and technical complexity, replacing the tst with igras as a public health intervention in resource-constrained settings is not recommended.

abstract: This guideline provides updated WHO recommendations for the programmatic management of tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) as part of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. It focuses on the prevention of active tuberculosis a
text:
who consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment item/9c30490a-8485-4eb7-8549-1209413fdc5f 10665-331170 world health organization  2020-02-25   tuberculosis, multidrug-resistant preventive health services health planning guideline this guideline provides updated who recommendations for the programmatic management of tuberculosis preventive treatment (tpt) as part of the who consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. it focuses on the prevention of active tuberculosis among people at increased risk of disease progression, particularly people living with hiv, household contacts of patients with tuberculosis and other vulnerable population groups. the document incorporates new evidence on shorter rifamycin-containing preventive treatment regimens and updates previous who guidance to improve the clarity, consistency and global applicability of recommendations.

developed in accordance with who guideline review committee requirements, the publication presents 18 evidence-based recommendations covering the identification of populations eligible for preventive treatment, exclusion of active tuberculosis, testing for latent tuberculosis infection, recommended preventive treatment regimens, monitoring and evaluation, and implementation considerations. recommendations were formulated using the grade approach, taking into account the certainty of evidence, effectiveness, safety, values and preferences, equity, resource implications, acceptability and feasibility. the guideline is intended to support national policy-makers, programme managers and health-care providers in strengthening tuberculosis prevention and advancing implementation of the who end tb strategy.

title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease
abstract: Tuberculosis remains one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent despite being largely preventable and curable. This updated WHO guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on systematic screening for tuberculosi

who consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease item/636231e5-1835-4721-8edb-6b2fecf4b5cd 10665-340255 world health organization  2021-03-22   algorithms guideline mass screening tuberculosis tuberculosis remains one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent despite being largely preventable and curable. this updated who guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on systematic screening for tuberculosis disease to support earlier diagnosis, timely initiation of treatment and reduced transmission. it revises the 2013 guidance in light of new evidence on the effectiveness of screening interventions and the performance of screening tools, using the grade approach to assess the certainty of evidence and the strength of recommendations. the document is intended to assist countries in planning and implementing screening strategies adapted to their epidemiological and health system contexts.

text:

text:
who guidelines for screening and treatment of precancerous lesions for cervical cancer prevention item/d6a6bd7e-b367-43d2-a82b-f5bd874d47fe 10665-94830 world health organization  2013-11-19   uterine cervical neoplasms precancerous conditions guideline these guidelines provide recommendations for screen-and-treat strategies to prevent cervical cancer by detecting and treating precancerous cervical lesions. the screen-and-treat approach bases treatment decisions on screening results, allowing treatment soon or ideally immediately after a positive test, rather than requiring histological confirmation. the guidelines compare strategies using human papillomavirus (hpv) testing, visual inspection with acetic acid (via), and cytology, linked to treatment with cryotherapy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure (leep). they are intended primarily to support policy-makers, programme managers and other health professionals in selecting appropriate cervical cancer prevention strategies according to available resources and existing programmes.

the handbook describes the cascade of care for tpt, including identification of target populations, exclusion of active tb disease, testing for tb infection, treatment options, management of adverse events, adherence support, monitoring and evaluation, and ethical considerations. it also provides operational guidance for contact investigation, integration of preventive services with active tb case finding and hiv services, health system strengthening, and resource mobilization. practical implementation tools, policy considerations and monitoring indicators are included to assist national tb programmes, policy-makers and health-care providers in adapting and scaling up tpt services in diverse epidemiological and health system settings.

تصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة: لغة مشتركة لوصف استخدامات التكنولوجيا الرقمية من أجل الصحة item/5cdd0488-c714-4542-9752-31cc9b4e9f9a 10665-379160 منظمة الصحة العالمية  2024-10-08   classification technology medical informatics telemedicine health services digital health تقدم هذه الطبعة الثانية من «تصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة» تصنيفاً معيارياً يصف كيفية استخدام التقنيات الرقمية لتلبية احتياجات الأفراد والنظم الصحية. وقد أعدت منظمة الصحة العالمية هذا التصنيف ليكون لغة مشتركة تدعم التواصل بين صانعي السياسات، ومديري البرامج الصحية، والباحثين، والمنفذين، ومطوري التكنولوجيا، وغيرهم من أصحاب المصلحة في مجال الصحة الرقمية. وينظم التصنيف التدخلات الصحية الرقمية حول قدرات تكنولوجية محددة صُممت لمعالجة التحديات التي تواجه النظم الصحية، ويربط هذه التدخلات بالخدمات وأنواع التطبيقات الرقمية التي تُستخدم لتنفيذها.

ويُحدِّث هذا المنشور ويوسِّع الطبعة الأولى الصادرة عام 2018 ليعكس التقدم في تقنيات الصحة الرقمية، وتطور ممارسات التنفيذ، والدروس المستفادة من استخدامها على المستوى العالمي. ويستند الإطار إلى ثلاثة محاور مترابطة: تحديات النظم الصحية، والتدخلات الصحية الرقمية، والخدمات وأنواع التطبيقات الرقمية. ويشمل تدخلات موجهة للأفراد، ولمقدمي الرعاية الصحية، ولمديري النظم الصحية، ولخدمات البيانات، إلى جانب فئات التطبيقات الرقمية ونظم المعلومات. ويهدف هذا التصنيف إلى دعم التخطيط والتنفيذ، وتحليل الاستثمارات، والبحوث، واعتبارات التشغيل البيني، وصياغة السياسات، وحوكمة مبادرات الصحة الرقمية، بما يعزز الاستخدام المنسق والفعال للتقنيات الرقمية في النظم الصحية.
